record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Let M be a closed manifold that is not a K(pi,1), let Sigma be a closed connected hypersurface in T*M, and let H be a Hamiltonian for which Sigma is the regular level H^{-1}(c). Is there an epsilon greater than zero such that, for almost every nearby energy value s in (c-epsilon,c+epsilon), the level H^{-1}(s) carries a contractible periodic orbit?

evidence.quote: almost all nearby levels contain a contractible periodic orbit

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold that is not aspherical (i.e., $M$ is not a $K(\pi,1)$-space, so some higher homotopy group $\pi_k(M)$ with $k\ge 2$ is nontrivial). Equip the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ with its standard symplectic structure $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the Liouville one-form. Let $\Sigma \subset T^*M$ be a closed connected smooth hypersurface, and let $H \colon T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$ be a smooth Hamiltonian such that $\Sigma = H^{-1}(c)$ is a regular level set for some $c \in \mathbb{R}$. A periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow of $H$ on a level set $H^{-1}(s)$ is called contractible if its underlying loop in $T^*M$ is contractible (equivalently, contractible in $M$ via the projection $T^*M \to M$).

Question: Does there exist $\varepsilon > 0$ such that, for almost every $s \in (c-\varepsilon, c+\varepsilon)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure, the level set $H^{-1}(s)$ carries a contractible periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow of $H$?
artifact.status_search_result: The contractible almost-existence problem in cotangent bundles is established in the symplectically aspherical setting (e.g., when $M$ is a $K(\pi,1)$), but for general closed manifolds $M$ that are not $K(\pi,1)$ the existence of contractible periodic orbits on almost every nearby energy level is listed as an open problem in symplectic topology. Search results confirm related results (relative Hofer–Zehnder capacity, noncontractible orbits for non-simply-connected $M$) but do not provide a resolution in the non-aspherical case.

status_evidence.title: Relative Hofer-Zehnder capacity and periodic orbits in twisted cotangent bundles
status_evidence.snippet: almost all low levels of a function on a geometrically bounded symplectically aspherical manifold carry contractible periodic orbits
status_evidence.claim: Contractible almost-existence is known in the symplectically aspherical setting; the non-aspherical case is not addressed here.

status_evidence.title: An almost existence theorem for non-contractible periodic orbits in cotangent bundles
status_evidence.snippet: almost every energy level carries a periodic orbit representing a non-trivial free homotopy class
status_evidence.claim: Counterpart almost-existence results are established for non-contractible classes when M is not simply connected, leaving the contractible case for non-aspherical M as a separate question.
